title: Adjuvant temozolomide after radiotherapy in IDH-mutant grade 3 astrocytoma
population: 751 adults with newly diagnosed 1p/19q non-codeleted grade 3 glioma; final molecular analysis identified 444 IDH-mutant tumours
summary: The final CATNON analysis after 10.9 years of median follow-up confirms that the major survival benefit comes from adjuvant temozolomide after radiotherapy in IDH-mutant tumours. Adjuvant TMZ improved OS with HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.42–0.69; P<0.0001), with median OS 12.5 years in the adjuvant-TMZ group. Concurrent TMZ did not significantly improve OS in IDH-mutant tumours (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.63–1.04; P=.09).
criticalReview: CATNON is a particularly important Absolute Effect trial because it separates the effect of concurrent from adjuvant temozolomide. The clinically important message is not simply that TMZ works, but that the survival benefit is driven by the post-radiotherapy adjuvant phase. NNT is not quantifiable for the primary endpoint because the mature overall-survival result is a time-to-event outcome best expressed through the hazard ratio and median survival; importantly, this does not mean the absolute effect is small. In IDH-mutant grade 3 astrocytoma, radiotherapy followed by 12 cycles of adjuvant TMZ is the evidence-based sequence, while concurrent TMZ has not demonstrated an additional OS benefit.
